title: Put the shown watch box back in a stepped showcase, slide both glass doors shut and push the plunger lock in
instruction: Close up the showcase after the showing. Put the watch box back on its marked spot on the lower step, at the front of the case, without knocking over or shifting the watches standing on the higher step; slide the inner glass door shut, then the outer glass door, and push the plunger lock on the outer door in until it latches. Then take your hands away.
context: Retail salespeople at locked cases (watches, jewellery, phones) show an item and lock the case again after every showing, many times a shift; O*NET 41-2031.00 Retail Salespersons (3,998,100 employed in 2025) lists 'Watch for and recognize security risks and thefts'; the U.S. Census Bureau counted 23,096 jewelry stores with employees in 2013 (County Business Patterns). Showcases are stepped toward the customer, so the item going back to the front step must pass over and between pieces on the step behind, each on a small stand that tips at a touch. The case is then shut back door first and the keyless plunger in the front door is pushed in: 'it takes only seconds to secure the bypassing doors' (CRL KML41). The robot carries a 9.7 x 7.6 x 7.1 cm box through a 22 cm door opening and a 14.2 cm gap between two stands onto a 12 cm spot, slides two glass panels against 3 N friction to within 5 mm of their stops, and pushes a 10 N spring plunger to full travel.
setup: A counter (the table) in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. On it stands a countertop showcase, 61 cm wide, 30.5 cm deep and 45.7 cm tall (Webstaurant 89129359 class: aluminium frame, 6 mm glass top, front and sides, a black velvet display deck 4 cm above the counter), its sliding back doors toward the arms, its back face 37 cm in front of the arm bases and centred between them. Inside, the display is a two-step stair facing the customer: the higher step is a white velvet riser 5.1 cm (2 in) high, 6.4 cm (2.5 in) deep and 58.4 cm wide, set right behind the door track, nearer the arms; the lower step is the deck in front of it, 20.5 cm deep. On the riser stand four watches, each strapped round a clear C-ring watch stand (2.2 x 1.5 x 3.9 in: a 5.6 x 3.8 cm base, 9.9 cm tall, 150 g with its watch: a 42 mm steel head, black bezel, blue or white dial, black or brown strap), their heads facing the customer, turned up, centred 6.2 cm in from the door line at 26 and 8 cm left of centre and 8 and 23 cm right of it; the two left stands leave a 14.2 cm gap. On the lower step a white tape square, 12 x 12 cm, marks the box's spot, centred 15.5 cm in from the door line and 17 cm left of centre, in line with that gap. Two 31 x 40 cm glass doors run in a double track: the inner (back-track) door shuts over the right half, the outer (front-track) door over the left half, overlapping 2 cm. At the start the outer door is slid fully right, in front of the inner door, and the inner door stands 6 cm open to the left, leaving a 22 cm opening at the left end. The outer door has a 15 mm round bar pull, 15 cm long, 7 cm from its overlapping edge, and a keyless push-plunger lock (CRL KML41 style) 12 cm up and 3.5 cm from that edge: a 16 mm head standing 17 mm out, which goes in 12 mm against a spring rising to 10 N and latches there. A single-watch case (9.7 x 7.6 x 7.1 cm, 150 g, burgundy leatherette) stands on the counter left of the showcase, 30 cm forward of the bases and 42 cm left of centre, its long side pointing forward. Real trial: any 24 x 12 x 18 in sliding-door countertop showcase with a push-plunger lock fitted, a 2 in acrylic riser, four watches on C-ring stands (each base outlined in thin tape on the riser), a single-watch case and white tape, filmed also by a front glass camera at deck height to see release height.
scoring: Box on its spot: the box's centre within 2.5 cm of the spot's centre on each axis, resting on the lower step (the deck, its base within 6 mm of it), upright within 10 degrees, and no gripper within 5 mm of it. Door shut: within 5 mm of its closed stop. Hands away: every point of both grippers (fingers, pads, palm and housing) and wrists (axis from link5 to the gripper) at least 1 cm outside the case's outline, its pull and lock head included. 0.25: box on its spot. 0.5: and the inner door shut. 0.75: and the outer door shut. 1.0: and the plunger latched, both hands away, all held for 2 s. Void, score 0, at any time: a watch stand on the higher step tilted over 20 degrees or its base moved over 1.5 cm from where it stood; or the box dropped or tipped over 45 degrees (simulator: its base falling over 8 mm in one 50 ms step, so any drop of 1.6 cm or more; real trial: the video shows it let go with its base over 1.5 cm above the deck, or falling free). The scorer reads end states, so door order is not checked.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz, GPU. Case frame and riser fixed to the counter. Doors: prismatic joints with end stops, 3 N track friction (assumed). Plunger: sprung slide, 10 N at full travel (assumed; a real KML41 may latch with a door open). Its catch is a rule: at full travel with both doors within 5 mm of their stops, plunger and doors are held, standing in for the tip at the inner door's edge; the tip has no collider. Box and stand masses and friction assumed.
scores: demo: 1.0 (step 815, 40.8 s); Dream-1: 0.0 (one valid run, 1,600 steps)
